# 4 Ezra Chapter 9 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 9:5 — "requital" vs. "recompense" vs. "payback"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-endings-in-requital-and-in-signs" | Archaic but accurate rendering of Latin retributio |
| LOGOS | "the endings in requital and in signs" | Same without hyphens |
| PNEUMA | "the endings are marked by payback and by signs" | More colloquial |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "The endings in requital and in signs" (LOGOS). "Requital" preserves the formal legal weight of retributio better than "payback."

---

## 9:11 — focus on the saved rather than the condemned

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "be-not-curious to-know how the-ungodly-shall-be-punished" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "be not curious to know how the ungodly shall be punished" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Don't waste your energy wondering how the wicked will be punished" | Paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Be not curious to know how the ungodly shall be punished" (LOGOS). The formal negative imperative preserves the instruction's tone.

---

## 9:13 — wave/drop comparison

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as-a-wave is-greater-than-a-drop" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "as a wave is greater than a drop" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the way a wave is bigger than a drop" | "Bigger" is slightly less elevated |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "As a wave is greater than a drop" (LOGOS). "Greater" is more precise than "bigger."

---

## 9:27 — the anaphoric description of God's attributes

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he-gives — for-he-is-a-giver..." with full repeated nouns | Maximum literalism |
| LOGOS | "he gives — for he is a giver..." | Clean and formal |
| PNEUMA | "He gives — because he is a giver..." | "Because" for "for" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS throughout this anaphoric list (vv. 27-28). The "for" of the Latin is the causal explanatory particle; LOGOS's "for" preserves this. The list should not be abbreviated.

---

## 9:45 — "the Mighty One" vs. "the Mighty"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "gave-great-glory to-the-Mighty" | Literal — Latin Potenti |
| LOGOS | "gave great glory to the Mighty One" | Adds "One" for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "gave enormous praise to the Mighty One" | "Enormous praise" slightly intensifies |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Gave great glory to the Mighty One" (LOGOS). The addition of "One" prevents the adjective from floating. "Great glory" is more precise than PNEUMA's "enormous praise."

---

## Total disagreements: 5
